title: India Opens NSIL Top Job to Private Sector Talent
excerpt: India's Department of Space invites private aerospace executives to lead NewSpace India Limited — a historic shift for the ISRO commercial arm.
body:
India's Department of Space formally opened the Chairman-cum-Managing Director post at NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) to private sector candidates in 2025 — a move that has put seasoned aerospace executives, including those from global giants like Boeing, squarely in the conversation.

**What the government announced:**
The Department of Space, Government of India, invited applications for the top leadership position of Chairman-cum-Managing Director (CMD) in NSIL, a wholly-owned Government of India CPSE, with the appointment on a deputation or contract basis for a period of five years. Crucially, the Search-cum-Selection Committee reserved the right to shortlist applicants for interview and was also free to identify and recommend any other person based on merit who may not have applied for the post. Private sector applicants were specifically invited to submit duly filled applications directly.

**Why Boeing's India footprint matters:**
Salil Gupte, President of Boeing India, leads the company's work in the region across commercial aviation, defence, and services, overseeing a team of 5,000 employees in India. He chairs the National Executive Board of AmCham India and the CII National Committee on Aerospace, making him one of the most networked aerospace executives in the country. Meanwhile, NSIL itself has grown into a formidable commercial player: NSIL launched 49 satellites on a commercial basis between 2023 and 2025, and NSIL is central to India's ambition to scale up its commercial space economy — expected to surge from roughly $13 billion today to potentially $77 billion by 2030.

**What to watch:**
The SCSC's final recommendation — and whether it breaks the tradition of appointing career government officials to NSIL's top post — will signal just how seriously India's space establishment intends to embrace private-sector leadership at a pivotal moment for its commercial launch ambitions.
